skill.description: Builds a Next.js workflow for designing and exporting iOS App Store marketing screenshots with phone mockups, slide planning, copy guidance, and html-to-image export.
skill.summary: Create exportable iOS App Store marketing screenshots with a guided Next.js generator.
skill.author: ParthJadhav

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, and TSX template literals. The only confirmed issue is the setup block that tells an agent to run package-manager commands, which is legitimate but can download dependencies and change the workspace. The screen-capture, system-reconnaissance, and binary-file findings were not supported by the reviewed context.

remediation.issue: Package-manager setup commands can download code and mutate the workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running scaffold or install commands, and explain which files and dependencies will change.

remediation.issue: Setup examples use latest package resolution for scaffolding and dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Pin known-good package versions or document a verified version set to reduce supply-chain drift.

content.value_statement: App Store screenshots need strong marketing copy, correct dimensions, and reliable exports. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a Next.js generator for polished iOS screenshot assets.
actual_capabilities: Collects required app assets, brand colors, font choices, feature priorities, and slide count before implementation.
Plans an App Store screenshot narrative with one clear selling point per slide.
Provides iPhone portrait export sizes for common Apple screenshot requirements.
Uses a pre-measured phone mockup and screen overlay constants for device framing.
Guides creation of a single Next.js page with preview, layout, and export logic.
Explains html-to-image export handling for fonts, images, offscreen rendering, and numbered filenames.
limitations: The guidance focuses on iPhone portrait screenshots and does not cover iPad, Android, or landscape formats.
The skill requires user-provided app screenshots, app icon, brand details, and feature priorities.
Export quality can depend on browser behavior, font loading, and local asset paths.
The included mockup is a static PNG asset, so teams should verify license and brand fit before release.

use_cases.title: Launch Screenshot Set
use_cases.description: Plan and build a first App Store screenshot set for a new iOS app launch.

use_cases.title: Marketing Refresh
use_cases.description: Turn existing app screens into clearer benefit-led marketing slides with stronger copy.

use_cases.title: Repeatable Export Workflow
use_cases.description: Create a reusable Next.js page that exports multiple sizes from one designed source.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Screenshot Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the app-store-screenshots skill to plan App Store screenshots for my iOS app. Ask me for the required assets, brand details, feature list, slide count, and style direction before writing code.

prompt_templates.title: Write Slide Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to create three headline options for each screenshot slide. Keep each headline focused on one idea, short enough for thumbnail viewing, and explain why each option works.

prompt_templates.title: Build the Generator Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to build a Next.js screenshot generator page from my approved slide plan. Use my provided assets, the included phone mockup, responsive previews, and export buttons for Apple iPhone portrait sizes.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Export Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to review my screenshot export workflow. Check font loading, image paths, offscreen rendering, html-to-image timing, sizing, filenames, and blank export fixes.

output_examples.input: A developer has a habit tracking app, five app screenshots, an app icon, green brand colors, and wants six App Store slides.
output: A six-slide narrative with a hero benefit, three focused feature slides, one trust slide, and one more-features slide.
Short headline options for each slide with suggested line breaks and visual emphasis.
A build plan for a Next.js generator using the phone mockup and Apple portrait export sizes.

output_examples.input: A product marketer wants existing screenshots to feel less like documentation and more like advertisements.
output: A revised slide sequence that gives each screenshot one clear selling point.
Recommendations for stronger copy, contrast slides, phone placement, and simplified decoration.
Export notes for consistent filenames and clean browser-based image generation.

output_examples.input: A design engineer has blank exports from html-to-image and needs a reliable export process.
output: A troubleshooting checklist for fonts, image loading, offscreen placement, timing, and capture order.
A recommendation to warm up exports before saving the final image.
A verification plan for preview scale, full-resolution output, and target dimensions.

best_practices: Approve the slide copy before building layouts, because weak copy reduces screenshot conversion.
Use one selling point per screenshot and vary phone placement across the full set.
Export from the largest required size first, then scale down for smaller Apple sizes.
anti_patterns: Do not turn each screenshot into a feature list with dense explanatory text.
Do not reuse the same phone layout on every slide unless the brand intentionally requires it.
Do not rely on plain black or white backgrounds when subtle branded depth would improve clarity.

faq.question: Does this skill create App Store screenshots automatically?
faq.answer: It guides an AI coding agent to build a generator. The user still provides app screenshots, icon, brand details, and approvals.

faq.question: Which app formats does it target?
faq.answer: It targets iPhone portrait App Store screenshots. The skill lists common Apple portrait dimensions for export.

faq.question: Does it include a phone mockup?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a pre-measured mockup.png file and overlay values for placing app screenshots inside the frame.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing Next.js app?
faq.answer: Yes. It can adapt an existing project, or it can scaffold a new Next.js project when the user approves setup commands.

faq.question: What export library does it use?
faq.answer: The skill recommends html-to-image because it handles CSS styling more reliably than html2canvas for this workflow.

faq.question: What should users prepare before starting?
faq.answer: Users should prepare real app screenshots, an app icon, brand colors, font choices, feature priorities, and a style direction.
